title: The angel of the mountains
hookLine: offered the two mountains brought down on his people, he refuses, hoping their children will worship Allah (Bukhari)

cards: Revenge, offered from the sky. That's where today's story goes. A few days ago we heard him tell Aisha about the day he was turned away and walked in a daze until he reached Qarn al-Tha'alib.
The same report in Sahih al-Bukhari doesn't stop there. When he came to himself, he says, he raised his head, and a cloud was shading him. He looked, and in it was Jibril.
Today: the angel of the mountains.

teach.b: In Bukhari's report he says, in effect: Allah has heard what your people said to you and how they answered you, and He has sent you the angel of the mountains, to order him as you wish.

Then the angel of the mountains himself calls out, greets him, and says: if you wish, I will bring the two Akhshabs together over them. Commentators explain the two Akhshabs as the two mountains on either side of Mecca.
Close them, and the people who mocked him are gone. Consider the timing. He has just lost his wife and his uncle.
He has been refused, jeered, chased. He's alone. And now he's offered what a wounded person might wish for: the power to make them pay, with heaven's permission.

teach.h: NO. I HOPE FOR THEIR CHILDREN.
teach.b: Rather, I hope that Allah will bring out from their descendants people who will worship Allah alone and associate nothing with Him.
Look at what he hoped for. Not that they would apologize, not even that they themselves would change.
He looked past the people in front of him to their children and grandchildren, people not yet born. That is a long view, taken on the worst day.
It fits the du'a from two days ago, which complained of weakness but cursed no one.
Muslims tell this story when they speak of the Prophet as a mercy, and Pickthall's Qur'an puts it this way in surah twenty-one: "We sent thee not save as a mercy for the peoples."

how: Muslims retell the angel of the mountains from Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim when speaking of the Prophet's mercy and restraint, and some read it alongside surah 21:107.

games.q: you've been rejected and chased. an angel offers to close two mountains over the people who did it. what do you say?
o: no; I hope their descendants will worship Allah.
wait until they've had one more chance.
games.why: in Bukhari he refuses outright and hopes for their children's children.

practice: Bring to mind someone who has hurt you, not the worst person, just someone real, and notice the part of you that would like to see them pay, without scolding it.
Then simply decline the revenge for today, which isn't forgiving everything or pretending it didn't happen.
Take his long view: wish well to someone connected to them, a child, a friend, a future version of them, and if you pray, ask Allah for good for them.

wordCard.voice: Jibril. He came with the angel of the mountains' offer to crush the people who had rejected him, and the Prophet refused, hoping for their children instead. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: 'the two Akhshabs', the two mountains on either side of Mecca named in the hadith.

carryVoice: Your line: hope for their children. Mercy, chosen on the hardest day. Day seven hundred fifty-three.
